acceptance: While a list or task prefix is typed or deleted on a source line (also a compact nested `- - [ ]`) the line keeps its list rail and the finished task is one item at its parent's depth plus one; nested item text blocks share their depth; literal content (indented code, `- [ ]task`, fences, an un-interrupting number) never becomes a task; a task transition reprojects every line of its item; bounded rhythm windows agree with the whole document.

A task toggle flips exactly the parser's checkbox span (wide, tab and nested) and back; Tab moves a whole item with its continuation and children under the previous item's content column (also the last item of a list directly before, such as a two-digit ordered parent) and Shift-Tab restores it; a first nested child keeps its place on Tab; a selected sibling group moves once with its children; Enter continues ordered tasks locally and continues a source continuation without inventing an item.

reason: The native editor parses Markdown with pulldown-cmark, which follows CommonMark: `2.` at column 0 after a list item starts a new ordered list. The product's Lezer parser keeps that line as a lazy continuation of the item, so it shows the number as literal text.
